newsitem.title: USA: Sale of Maine Yankee being negotiated.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Maine Yankee being negotiated.

text.p: The owners of the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant are negotiating a possible sale of the troubled facility, board chairman David Flanagan said Wednesday.
Flanagan declined to release the name of the potential buyer for the 910-megawatt facility in Wiscasset, said the potential purchaser was interested in buying all the ownership shares.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
Maine Yankee president Mike Sellman said Entergy Corp , which has been managing Maine Yankee's operations for the utility owners since February, is not the potential buyer.

Maine Yankee has been off-line since December 6 for a variety of safety problems, including misrouted electrical cables. The plant is not expected to resume operation until late summer at the earliest.

Maine Yankee pledged in December to spend $38 million in 1997 to address equipment and safety problems cited by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, which has placed the plant on its Watch List of nuclear facilities needing closer inspection.
